note: Placeholder imagery for design review only. Every entry must be replaced with real Medelis photography, or removed, before production. See docs/03-stack-and-setup.md §5.
revision: v3 — 2026-08-11. The v2 set was sterilization-era (cleanrooms, gowned operators, an empty warehouse) and read as an operating theatre, which is wrong for a pharmaceutical marketing and distribution company. Replaced entirely with dispensary, stock and pack-shot imagery.
grade: Per docs/02-design-system.md §8: slight desaturation (~85%), lifted midtones, shadows cooled toward the new primary #0D47A1. Deliberately much lighter than the v2 grade, which desaturated to 14% and was a large part of why the page read dull.
pipeline: sharp: resize(fit=cover) -> modulate({saturation, brightness}) -> composite(#0D47A1 @ soft-light, low opacity) -> linear(1.04,-6) -> webp(q80)

images.description: Curved dispensary drawer cabinets in perspective
images.why: Reads unmistakably as a pharmacy dispensary, has real depth, and carries no branding at all — which matters most in the page's most scrutinised slot.

images.description: Stock shelving filled with medicine cartons
images.why: Says 'we hold stock', which is the single thing a distributor most wants to see. Carton text is present but illegible at display size.

images.description: White pharmaceutical bottles with coloured caps on clean shelving
Unbranded blister strip of orange tablets, close crop
images.why: Graded closest to natural because a pack shot has to read as real product. The warm orange is also the one thing on the page that isn't blue, which stops the palette going monotone.

images.description: Amber bottle with unbranded white tablets

rejected.reason: Third-party branding clearly legible — 'SANDOZ' and named drug labels. Breaches §5.1 rule 3.
